cohort: 226 infants (46 IDMs and 138 infants born to unaffected mothers) admitted to the Level II Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU)
finding: A significantly higher proportion of infants born to diabetic mothers experienced adverse neonatal outcomes, including respiratory disease, NICU admission, phototherapy, congenital heart defects, and myocardial hypertrophy, compared to infants of unaffected mothers.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the most frequent mode of delivery among mothers with diabetes.
